title: ui lib test binary dies with SIGSEGV on the Linux runner uma (post-merge run 45046106061, commit 87fb95f29)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happened
Post-merge run 45046106061, second attempt, commit 87fb95f29 (the merge of PR #3363, the GPU compute seam), runner `uma`:

```
[1074] ui suites: lib
     (cwd ui) target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/4767f73a25f19268/out/camcraft_ui-4767f73a25f19268 --test-threads=16 (direct, from the build's cargo JSON artifacts)
     FAIL in 4s exit -1 (killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV), core dumped)
  wall 42.2 min, 1100 step(s), 1 failed, 0 stalled
```

The other 1099 steps are green, the other 25 ui suites included. The log has no test name and no panic text: the process died 4 seconds after its start.

## What is known
- The run of 054c1e24b, a later commit that contains 87fb95f29, is green on the runner `wopr-2` (run 45050724895). The run of deb5364ee, the commit before 87fb95f29, is green on the runner `dude`.
- Thus the crash is not seen on each runner or in each run. The cause is not known. It can be the runner `uma`, or a fault that shows at intervals.
- 87fb95f29 is the first commit in which `camcraft-ui` links `camcraft-gpu` and `wgpu`. Check first if a ui lib test, or code that starts with the test binary, gets a GPU adapter or loads a graphics driver on a runner with no display.
- An earlier issue with the same sign: #2807 (closed), "ui test binary egui_app stops with SIGSEGV at intervals on the Linux runner".

## Why P2
A crash of a test binary makes the gate of `main` red at intervals. If the crash is in product code (a GPU probe at start), a user on Linux can get it too. Then the priority is P1.

## Wanted
- Find the test or the start code that crashes: run the ui lib binary on `uma` some times with `--test-threads=1` and with `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`, and read the core dump if the runner keeps it.
- If the cause is a GPU probe with no adapter or no display: the probe must give a named reason and the CPU path, never a crash (Prime Directive).
- A test that pins the fix, or a recorded reason if the fault is in the runner image.
